_disclosure: PRE-AUTHORED, BOUNDED ACTION LIBRARY. Corrective Replanning selects from this list and never generates free-form clinical text. Every entry is derived from the OCHRA-grounded error definitions in agents/error_detection/knowledge.py — specifically from each category's own normal_indicators, which describe what correct technique looks like, so a corrective action is the stated inverse of the observed deviation rather than novel clinical advice.

_provenance.tier_meaning: Derived from published OCHRA error descriptions rather than quoted from a clinical guideline. Tier 1 would be a direct guideline recommendation; tier 3 would be unsourced authoring. Recorded honestly because these are surgical suggestions and the strength of their sourcing is part of what a reviewer needs to judge them.
_provenance.review_status: Not reviewed by a practising surgeon. This is architectural demonstration content, not validated clinical decision support.

_schema.keyed_by: error_category — the six CARES-collapsed OCHRA groupings
_schema.action_id: stable, referenced by corrective_trajectory node ids
_schema.rationale: why, traced to the OCHRA indicator it inverts
_schema.verification_check: the observable that confirms the action took effect — what divergence detection later compares against
_schema.inverts_indicator: the specific error_indicator this action addresses

multiple_attempts.action: Fully withdraw the instrument and re-plan the approach before the next attempt
multiple_attempts.rationale: OCHRA distinguishes a legitimate retry, which is preceded by a clear regrasp or reposition, from repetition driven by a failed prior attempt. Backing out fully converts the former into the latter.
multiple_attempts.verification_check: The next attempt is preceded by a visible withdrawal and reposition, not an immediate re-approach to the same point
multiple_attempts.inverts_indicator: The same piercing/grasp point is attempted 2+ times in quick succession

multiple_attempts.action: Move to a fresh tissue entry point rather than re-attempting the same one
multiple_attempts.rationale: Repeated attempts at one point accumulate local trauma, and a point that has already failed twice is unlikely to succeed on a third identical attempt.
multiple_attempts.verification_check: The subsequent attempt targets a visibly different point on the tissue
multiple_attempts.inverts_indicator: Instrument tip re-approaches the same tissue target repeatedly without progress

out_of_view.action: Re-centre the endoscope so all active working tips are in frame before continuing
out_of_view.rationale: OCHRA's normal state is that working tips of all active instruments remain in frame; restoring the view restores the surgeon's own error detection.
out_of_view.verification_check: All active instrument tips are visible in frame in subsequent windows
out_of_view.inverts_indicator: An instrument's tip is occluded or off-frame during active tissue interaction

out_of_view.action: Pause the pass and bring the needle back into view before completing it
out_of_view.rationale: A needle that leaves frame mid-pass is unaccounted for, which is both a technique problem and a retained-item risk.
out_of_view.verification_check: The needle is visible and under instrument control before the pass resumes
out_of_view.inverts_indicator: Needle disappears from frame while a throw/pass is in progress

out_of_view.action: Confirm the needle is accounted for before moving to the next step
out_of_view.rationale: Directly addresses the retained-foreign-body pathway that follows from losing sight of a needle.
out_of_view.verification_check: The needle is visibly located and controlled before the next sub-step begins
out_of_view.inverts_indicator: Needle disappears from frame while a throw/pass is in progress

needle_handling.action: Release and re-grasp the needle at or near the swage, perpendicular to the driver
needle_handling.rationale: OCHRA's normal state is a stable grasp at or near the swage with perpendicular orientation; a tip grasp or steep angle is what makes the needle slip or bend.
needle_handling.verification_check: The needle is held at mid-body or swage with a stable perpendicular orientation in subsequent windows
needle_handling.inverts_indicator: Needle grasped very close to the tip, or at a steep/awkward angle relative to the driver

needle_handling.action: Re-establish control of the needle before advancing it further through tissue
needle_handling.rationale: Advancing a needle that is already slipping deepens the tissue injury the slip caused.
needle_handling.verification_check: The needle stays under instrument control through the remainder of the pass
needle_handling.inverts_indicator: Needle visibly slips or drops while partially embedded in tissue

needle_handling.action: Stop and locate the needle before proceeding if control was lost
needle_handling.rationale: A dropped needle is a retained-item risk that compounds the longer the case continues without accounting for it.
needle_handling.verification_check: The needle is visibly recovered and under control before the next sub-step
needle_handling.inverts_indicator: Needle visibly slips or drops while partially embedded in tissue

tissue_handling.action: Reduce traction force and re-assess tissue response before continuing
tissue_handling.rationale: OCHRA's normal state is that tissue returns to its resting position and colour after release; blanching or tenting indicates force beyond what the step requires.
tissue_handling.verification_check: Blanching or tenting resolves and tissue returns to resting colour after release
tissue_handling.inverts_indicator: Visible blanching, tenting, or tearing at a grasp point

tissue_handling.action: Release and re-grasp with a broader tissue purchase to distribute force
tissue_handling.rationale: A narrow grasp concentrates force at a point; spreading the purchase lowers local pressure for the same effective traction.
tissue_handling.verification_check: The subsequent grasp shows no localised blanching at the contact point
tissue_handling.inverts_indicator: Repeated forceful re-grasping of the same tissue region

tissue_handling.action: Re-orient the direction of traction to align with the plane being developed
tissue_handling.rationale: Force disproportionate to the sub-step is often a direction problem rather than a magnitude one, and pulling across a plane rather than along it tears rather than exposes.
tissue_handling.verification_check: Traction direction visibly follows the dissection plane in subsequent windows
tissue_handling.inverts_indicator: Traction direction/force appears disproportionate to what the sub-step requires

suture_handling.action: Stop and clear the suture entanglement before the next throw
suture_handling.rationale: OCHRA's normal state is a suture running cleanly with no visible loop or twist; throwing over an entanglement locks the fault into the closure.
suture_handling.verification_check: The suture line runs cleanly with no visible loop or twist before the next throw
suture_handling.inverts_indicator: Visible loop, twist, or entanglement in the suture line

suture_handling.action: Adjust suture tension to match the tissue gap being approximated
suture_handling.rationale: Both slack and over-tension are named deviations: slack fails to appose, over-tension strangles the edge.
suture_handling.verification_check: Tension appears even and proportionate to the tissue gap in subsequent windows
suture_handling.inverts_indicator: Suture is noticeably slack or over-tensioned relative to the tissue gap

suture_handling.action: Run the suture through fully before placing the next throw
suture_handling.rationale: Removes accumulated slack in one deliberate motion rather than mid-throw, which is when entanglement usually forms.
suture_handling.verification_check: No mid-task pause to manually clear suture in subsequent windows
suture_handling.inverts_indicator: The surgeon pauses to manually clear/untangle suture mid-task

instrument_control.action: Increase separation between the instrument arms before resuming
instrument_control.rationale: OCHRA's normal state is adequate spacing between simultaneously-active instruments; clashing arms make both trajectories unpredictable.
instrument_control.verification_check: No instrument-to-instrument contact in subsequent windows
instrument_control.inverts_indicator: Visible clash or collision between the two instrument arms

instrument_control.action: Move the idle instrument clear of the active working field
instrument_control.rationale: An instrument parked in the working field obstructs both the view and the other arm's path.
instrument_control.verification_check: The idle instrument is visibly clear of the active field in subsequent windows
instrument_control.inverts_indicator: One instrument idles awkwardly in a way that obstructs the other's working path

instrument_control.action: Slow the motion and re-centre the instruments before the next manoeuvre
instrument_control.rationale: Overshooting and corrective micro-movements compound; resetting to a neutral position restores a predictable starting point.
instrument_control.verification_check: Instrument trajectories appear smooth and deliberate in subsequent windows
instrument_control.inverts_indicator: Jerky, overshooting, or corrective micro-movements beyond normal tremor filtering
